paper_title: Improved constraints on non-Newtonian forces at 10 microns
coupling_convention: α (dimensionless coupling strength relative to gravity), as plotted on the y-axis of the Yukawa-force exclusion plot
notes: Paper presents 95% confidence exclusion limits on Yukawa-type fifth forces parameterized as α (strength relative to gravity) vs λ (range). Data extracted from Table V (95% exclusion α values). The coupling type ScalarNucleon is appropriate because this experiment constrains Yukawa-type interactions between macroscopic masses (nucleon-mediated fifth force), which is the canonical fifth-force/equivalence-principle test. The paper explicitly states '95 percent confidence exclusion of forces with |α| > 14,000 at λ = 10 microns' in the abstract. Mass values converted from microns to eV using λ[eV] = 1.240e-6 eV·m / λ[m]. This represents a significant improvement (factor of ~3) over their previous Stanford 2 results and is the best bound in the 5–15 μm range at the time of publication. | selector: figure_vision over table (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 61)) | Vision: This paper reports improved constraints on Yukawa-type fifth forces using cryogenic micro-cantilevers. The exclusion plot (FIG. 9) shows the lower boundary of the excluded region in the (λ, α) plane, where λ is the range in micrometers and α is the coupling strength relative to gravity. The x-axis has been converted from micrometers to eV using the relation m[eV] = ℏc/λ ≈ 1.240e-6 eV·m / λ[m]. The y-axis shows α directly as plotted. The boundary traces the Stanford 3 result (present work), which represents the best constraint in the 5–15 μm range with 95% confidence exclusion of forces with |α| > 14,000 at λ = 10 μm. The coupling type is ScalarNucleon because the paper explicitly discusses Yukawa-type corrections to the Newtonian potential mediated by light scalar particles, which couple to nucleon mass. Data points were extracted by visual tracing of the lower exclusion boundary from the plot, sampling more densely at corners and kinks where the slope changes. | Calibration: Vision calibration: ×1e-2 (factor=1.00e-02, reason=spot-check verify/stage2, raw_ratio=0.01)
